lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: knowing local rules before applying

objective: Learners re-verify the working-age and permit rules researched earlier this year against a second, current source, and add any additional first-job rule (such as required breaks or how soon pay must be provided) relevant to their location, so the capstone portfolio's rule check is current rather than months old.
scenario: The learner takes the working-age rules recorded earlier this year, checks them again against a second, current source to confirm nothing has changed, and researches one additional first-job rule for their location, recording both with sources.
safetyNotes: Rules are re-checked against a current source rather than assumed to be unchanged from earlier research.
materials: working-age rule notes from earlier this year
access to a current source for re-verification, or the provided reference summary

tasks.directions: Before re-checking, restate the working-age rules you recorded earlier this year.

prompts.text: Restate what you previously found about working-age rules for your location.

tasks.directions: Re-verify those rules against a second, current source, and note whether anything changed.

prompts.text: Record what your second source says and whether it matches your earlier finding.
I used a genuinely different source than my original research earlier this year.

tasks.directions: Research one additional first-job rule for your location not covered by your earlier research.

prompts.text: Record the additional rule you found, what it means practically, and your source.
Did re-checking change anything, and either way, what does that tell you about how often information like this should be reverified?

remediation: If a learner's re-verification uses the same source as the original research rather than a genuinely independent one, reteach by requiring a different type of source (for example, an official page the first time and a different kind of resource the second time) before the re-check counts as complete.
extension: Have the learner research how these rules would differ for a job in a genuinely different location (such as a different state or country) and compare the two rule sets.
